tests: Kind assignment. Technical, behavioural and domain requirements sit side by side, several of them worded so the obvious reading is wrong.
jd:
Clinical Data Engineer — Aster Trials (Cambridge)

Aster runs data infrastructure for phase II and III oncology trials.

Requirements:
• 3+ years with Python and pandas for clinical data transformation
• Working knowledge of CDISC SDTM and ADaM standards
• Experience with GCP BigQuery or a comparable warehouse
• You will present findings to clinicians who are not engineers, so you must be able to explain a data quality problem without jargon
• Comfortable pushing back on a study team when a requested analysis would not be statistically sound
• Understanding of GxP validation and why an audit trail matters
• Familiarity with oncology endpoints such as PFS and ORR

Nice to have:
• Experience with R
• Prior work at a CRO
notes: The interesting ones: 'explain a data quality problem without jargon' is behavioural despite sitting in a technical list and mentioning data quality; 'pushing back when an analysis would not be statistically sound' is behavioural, not domain, even though it names statistics; CDISC, GxP and oncology endpoints are domain, not technical, though they read like tooling. 'Experience with R' is a one-letter label and exists to catch a scorer that matches substrings carelessly.
